arabic.text: وَٱلْفَجْرِ (١) وَلَيَالٍ عَشْرٍۢ (٢) وَٱلشَّفْعِ وَٱلْوَتْرِ (٣) وَٱلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَسْرِ (٤) هَلْ فِى ذَٰلِكَ قَسَمٌۭ لِّذِى حِجْرٍ (٥) أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ (٦)

head: Ayah

rows: And [by] the even [number] and the odd

Is there [not] in [all] that an oath [sufficient] for one of perception?
Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Aad -

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 89:1-6 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Who were 'Aad (89:6)? Say one thing you know from the ayat.
questions.a: A people Allah destroyed for their arrogance; they built Iram with lofty pillars (89:7).

questions.q: Find the meem sakinah in 89:6 and name its rule.
What does Allah swear by in 89:1?
Think again: Al-Fajr begins with Allah swearing by the dawn. What changes in the world at dawn?
questions.a: Darkness ends, light comes, birds wake, we pray Fajr: a new start that Allah brings every day.
